interpretations.mapping: Operationalize 'what would we need to observe' as attribution-by-control on the bands export. Control: bands="none", lean="firm" — after is_settled() returns true, read at_rim() and rest_azimuth_deg(); the control earns the later claim only if the ball rests at the rim near azimuth 0 (the verdict plate's RESTS DOWNHILL branch). Condition: bands="pair", lean="firm" — read rest_azimuth_deg(), on_band(), nearest_band_edge_deg(). The band is 'forbidding' iff the condition's rest azimuth leaves the pair arc centered at 14.0 deg (half-width 28.0 deg, from _band_arcs()) while on_band() is false: refusal measured as the control-to-condition angular difference.
assumptions: The fixed-step accumulator (FIXED_H = 1.0 / 240.0) makes the two runs integrate identically regardless of engine tick rate — the script's own stated claim, assumed here rather than treated as evidence — so control and condition differ only by the bands export

The deliberate 14-degree offset of the band arcs off the downhill axis breaks the knife-edge symmetry the same way every run (the script's stated design rationale, assumed here), so one condition run is representative
is_settled() true without the timeout suffix means a genuine rest, not a stall
exclusions: Says nothing about the belt value or the ON THE FORBIDDEN verdict branch
Does not vary lean; the gradient of consultability is a separate interpretation
Does not test headset legibility of the Label3D plate or the hall's creature encounter
Does not claim the deflection angle equals any particular number — only that it exits the band's sector

interpretations.mapping: Operationalize the tutorial's presentation-versus-stored-data lesson (its read()/COVER/REVEAL deep-copy discipline) on the artifact's own two layers: the Label3D plate text built by _verdict() is presentation; rest_azimuth_deg(), rest_rho_m(), on_band(), at_rim() and nearest_band_edge_deg() are the stored, probe-readable claim. A verdict counts as measured iff the azimuth printed in the plate's RESTS CLEAR / RESTS DOWNHILL / ON THE FORBIDDEN strings equals rest_azimuth_deg() recomputed from the settled shell, and the plate's color choice (band_color vs clear_color vs ball_color) agrees with on_band() and at_rim(). The hall's four readouts fail this test by design (their percentages are configuration); the dish is the proposed counter-exhibit.
assumptions: The readable methods are the authoritative record, as the tutorial treats claims.records as authoritative over the returned view
_verdict() and the readable methods are called on the same settled state (physics is stopped by set_physics_process(false) at settle)
exclusions: Does not ask whether the deflection is physically correct, only whether display and record cohere
Excludes timing questions (SETTLE_TICKS, TIMEOUT_TICKS) except as a precondition
Does not compare against the hall's situated_readout code or modify any hall exhibit

interpretations.mapping: Operationalize 'a rule that acts on a body' as a threshold question on the lean export: at which of its four values {"level", "faint", "firm", "steep"} is the band rule ever consulted? From the script's own comment, the minimum of K*rho^2 - S*x sits at x = S/2K, interior unless S > 2*K*R: with DISH_K = 0.9 and dish_radius = 0.16 the threshold is S = 0.288, so LEANS "level" (0.0) and "faint" (0.12) predict a rest short of the rim with at_rim() false and the bands never met — "level" at the centre (predicted rest_rho_m() of 0.0, under _verdict()'s 0.05 m threshold: the CENTERED branch, 'the bands were never met'), "faint" at a predicted rest_rho_m() of 0.0667 m, interior but above that threshold, so the predicted plate branch is RESTS MID-DISH ('the bowl holds it short of the bands') — while "firm" (0.34) and "steep" (0.55) predict the rim is the constraint. Sweep lean with bands="pair" and read at_rim(), rest_rho_m(), on_band() per value: the prediction is that the rule exists at every lean but acts on the body only past the threshold.
assumptions: The point-mass paraboloid arithmetic approximates the verlet shell's rest well enough to classify interior versus rim (the shell's ball_radius = 0.06 offset is ignored by the hand calculation)
GRIP = 0.12 is low enough that friction does not hold the ball interior at firm or steep
exclusions: Does not predict the exact deflection azimuth at firm or steep, only rim-reached versus rim-never-consulted
Does not vary bands; pair is held as the fixed band shape
Makes no claim about the belt's no-escape geometry or about VR encounter quality

reference_fixture.description: Pen-and-paper rest-position arithmetic on the tilted paraboloid y = DISH_K * rho^2 - S * x, treating the ball as a point on the surface (the shell radius is deliberately ignored and logged as debt). Part 1 classifies each lean value as interior-minimum (rim never consulted) or wall-constrained, against the threshold S = 2 * DISH_K * dish_radius. Part 2, for lean="firm" with bands="pair", compares the dish height at the band face on the downhill axis against the rim height at the band's near edge (azimuth -14 deg), to predict whether deflection to the clear arc is energetically preferred. All outputs are predictions; no run has occurred under this record, and none of the registry's descriptive numbers were used.
expected: level (S=0.0): x* = 0.0 / 1.8 = 0.0000 m -> interior; predicted CENTERED, rim never consulted

faint (S=0.12): x* = 0.12 / 1.8 = 0.0667 m -> interior (0.0667 < 0.16); predicted rest short of the rim, bands never met — and since 0.0667 m is above _verdict()'s 0.05 m CENTERED threshold, the predicted plate branch with bands present is RESTS MID-DISH, not CENTERED
firm (S=0.34): x* = 0.34 / 1.8 = 0.1889 m -> past the wall (0.1889 > 0.16); the rim is the constraint
steep (S=0.55): x* = 0.55 / 1.8 = 0.3056 m -> past the wall (0.3056 > 0.16); the rim is the constraint

firm + pair: rim point at azimuth -14 deg sits 0.0047 m LOWER than the downhill-axis point at the band face (-0.0297 vs -0.0250), so the prediction is deflection out of the band's sector to a clear rest (on_band() false), not a park against the wall
reference_fixture.arithmetic: Interior minimum along the downhill axis (z = 0): y(x) = DISH_K * x^2 - S * x, dy/dx = 0 at x* = S / (2 * DISH_K) = S / 1.8. Interior iff x* < dish_radius = 0.16, i.e. iff S < 2 * 0.9 * 0.16 = 0.288. level: 0.0/1.8 = 0.0000 (interior). faint: 0.12/1.8 = 0.0667 (interior). firm: 0.34/1.8 = 0.1889 (exterior). steep: 0.55/1.8 = 0.3056 (exterior). Clear-arc preference at lean=firm, bands=pair: band face radius = dish_radius - BAND_DEPTH = 0.16 - 0.06 = 0.10. Point A, downhill axis at the face: y_A = 0.9 * 0.10^2 - 0.34 * 0.10 = 0.009 - 0.034 = -0.0250 m. Point B, rim at the band's near edge, azimuth -14 deg (pair arc spans 14 +/- 28 deg, i.e. -14 to +42): x_B = 0.16 * cos(14 deg) = 0.16 * 0.9703 = 0.15525, rho_B = 0.16, y_B = 0.9 * 0.16^2 - 0.34 * 0.15525 = 0.02304 - 0.05278 = -0.0297 m. y_B - y_A = -0.0047 m: the clear edge is 4.7 mm lower, so sliding past the band's edge is predicted to be preferred over resting on the forbidden.

learning_debt.question: The fixture's arithmetic treats the ball as a point on the paraboloid; the actual body is a verlet pressure shell of radius 0.06 with GRIP 0.12. Do the interior/exterior classifications (x* = S/1.8 vs 0.16) and the 4.7 mm clear-arc preference survive the finite, frictional body?

questions.question: Can a readout's verdict be earned by measurement instead of supplied by configuration — and can a learner, before the run, reconstruct that verdict by hand from the apparatus's published constants, so that the printed azimuth is a prediction they made rather than a number they were handed?

When a rule acts on a body rather than being printed above it, what observation separates a constraint that actually refused the body from one the body never met — and what control condition must be witnessed before the red bands may be called forbidding at all?

reconsider_if: The control run (bands="none", lean="firm") does not rest at the rim near azimuth 0 — at_rim() false or |rest_azimuth_deg()| large after is_settled() — which would break attribution-by-control and show the point-mass fixture misclassifies the finite shell (ball_radius 0.06, GRIP 0.12)

Either condition reaches TIMEOUT_TICKS (the plate appends "(still moving at timeout)" / _timed_out true) in the hall: the verdict would then be a fact about a timeout, not a rest, and the settle criterion (SETTLE_EPS, SETTLE_TICKS) needs rework before any companion claim

Two launches of the same hall settle bands="pair" to different sides or different verdict branches: the 14-degree symmetry break would be insufficient in situ, and 'where you come to rest is the shape of what refused you' stops being a reproducible answer

The hall's map token is found to carry bands/lean values that apply_grid_config() silently fails to set (BANDS_SET/LEANS membership checks fail and the dish stays at defaults "pair"/"firm"): the installed encounter would then differ from the configured one and the comparison must move to a bench scene

final.md's own proposed next experiment (panels revealing 'a distinct criterion and the observation it used') is implemented, changing what the bound passage asks and possibly superseding the dish's role as the hall's only earned verdict
